data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density similar vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, Eg5 inhibitors, Microtubule stabilizers

observations.finding: Marked mitotic arrest phenotype. Treated fields show ~30-40% small, round, intensely fluorescent yellow-white cells vs <2% in DMSO f_a63b63b85186. DMSO confluent monolayer of flat interphase cells; treated sparse with many rounded detached-appearing cells and small clusters (e.g., f_55e7ca28ae81 center). Interphase cell number reduced but total objects similar.

Beta-tubulin (green) strongly increased in intensity and heterogeneity/texture. DMSO: dim diffuse filamentous network. Treated: very bright punctate spindles/asters in round cells plus brighter interphase fibers, high contrast.
F-actin (red) brighter and more heterogeneous, mostly cortical rim around interphase cells and very bright ring around rounded mitotic cells vs uniform DMSO cortical belts.

DNA (blue) brighter overall and integrated per-cell increased; many condensed mitotic chromosomes (white-yellow overlap) and enlarged/irregular interphase nuclei, some bilobed, vs uniform small oval DMSO nuclei. Solidity slightly reduced / irregular contour.
No microtubule loss or actin depolymerization seen; tubulin and actin networks preserved in interphase cells, arguing against destabilizer/disruptor.

notable_cells.why: example bright doublet mitotic figures - two adjacent intensely yellow-white round cells with blue condensed chromosomes surrounded by red cortical actin
cluster of ~12 bright yellow-white mitotic cells - hallmark of mitotic arrest, not seen in DMSO
interphase cell with enlarged irregular/lobed blue nuclei and bright green tubulin - enlarged DNA content
group of polyploid-like cells with multiple blue nuclear lobes and intense tubulin/actin

candidate_mechanisms.why: High mitotic index + increased nuclear DNA mean/integrated and decreased solidity indicate polyploid/G2-M block and failed cytokinesis with intact tubulin/actin, classic Aurora phenotype. Strongly increased tub_std/glcm_contrast reflects bright spindle foci rather than bundles. Eg5 inhibitors and Microtubule stabilizers are close antimitotic mimics with same composite readout and cannot be excluded at 1024px composite-only resolution.

Alternative monopolar spindle arrest - also gives numerous small bright round mitotics, increased tub_mean/tub_std and increased DNA content. Spindle monopolarity not resolvable without grayscale tubulin/DNA channels.
Explains large z~28-40 increase in tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast (increased polymer). Would also cause mitotic arrest; but interphase bundles not clearly seen at this resolution.

report.uncertainty: Composites only, no grayscale channels, limited to 1024px. Mitotic spindle morphology (monoaster vs multipolar vs normal) and nuclear multilobation cannot be scored definitively, so Aurora vs Eg5 vs stabilizer cannot be distinguished. Single concentration 1.0uM, short 24h. Actin/tubulin increases may be secondary to mitotic rounding. No support for Actin disruptors, Microtubule destabilizers, DNA damage/replication, Cholesterol-lowering, etc.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth = Eg5 inhibitors. Submitted conclusion = Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62. Incorrect.

What the evidence got right:
- Correctly identified an antimitotic mitotic-arrest phenotype, not DNA damage, actin, protein synthesis/degradation, etc. This was supported by: density similar vs DMSO by microscopist, no cell loss - High dose w_246fbe6008 (1 µM) 295 cells, mid dose w_2eeef82f69 295 cells, low dose w_6d52bef633 416 cells - consistent with arrest not acute cytotoxicity; strongly decreased nuc_solidity z=-28.3 at 1 µM, -19.1 at 0.03 µM, -15.2 even at 0.001 µM and -15.6 at 0.3 µM plus decreased form_factor, and elevated nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.8 at 0.03 µM and +14.3 at 0.001 µM.
- describe_phenotype correctly kept both Microtubule stabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors (and Aurora) as candidates on 4 fields. compare_to_reference_atlas was also correctly equivocal: 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 4/10 Eg5 inhibitors. That near-tie should have been the central uncertainty.
- Correctly downweighted Microtubule destabilizers, Actin disruptors, DNA damage/replication based on increased not decreased tubulin metrics.

What misled and why:
- Over-interpretation of tubulin intensity/texture as stabilizer-specific. w_246fbe6008 tub_mean z=+28.5, tub_std z=+19.4 at 0.03 µM, tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2 at 1 µM, and dose_response rho=+1.00 p=0 for both tub_mean (e8) and tub_glcm_contrast (e11) over 4 wells/4 doses were taken as selective polymerization/bundling signature. In this image-based assay Eg5 inhibition producing monopolar asters with dense focal tubulin also drives very high tub_mean, tub_std and contrast. There was no direct literature in this run comparing the two phenotypes - PubMed search 'microtubule stabilizer vs Eg5 inhibitor phenotype' returned 0 hits - so the claim that this magnitude is discriminating was unsupported. I anchored on the extreme z=+40.2 and monotonic rho without considering the overlap.
- Under-weighting of Eg5 support. e4 included Eg5 inhibitors among microscopist candidates and e5 gave 4/10 Eg5 nearest references. In update_hypotheses I listed e2 and e11 as "contradicting" Eg5, but extreme tub contrast does not contradict Eg5; monastrol, the prototype small-molecule inhibitor of spindle bipolarity, produces monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest PMID 10542155, PMID 10973989, and is an allosteric inhibitor of Eg5 PMID 12323373, PMID 15665380, PMID 12525161. Image-based profiling alone is known to conflate these mitotic MoAs without spindle-pole resolution PMID 24997502.
- Ignoring flat/inconsistent DNA/large-nucleus dose responses that argued against a classic stabilizer polyploidy progression. nuc_dna_integrated rho=0.00 p=1 (e9) over the same 4 wells was flat - high already at the lowest dose tested - and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (e10) was non-significant negative. That does not support a graded stabilizer-induced G2/M->polyploidy increase and was not incorporated as contradicting evidence for stabilizers.
- Acquisition choices: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.0003-1 µM available but I only acquired 4 wells (0.001, 0.03, 0.3, 1 µM) with n=1 per dose. Dose_response with n=4 and reported p=0 is over-confident and cannot be interpreted as strong monotonic proof. No high-resolution confocal tubulin/DNA spindle imaging or phospho-histone H3 assay was acquired to distinguish stabilizer bundles/multipolar spindles from Eg5 monopolar spindles, which was explicitly noted in the "next_experiment_if_this_were_a_real_lab" but should have been done before submitting. Protocol lookup after unblinding confirmed AZ-C has no PubChem/ChemBL structure curated (BBBC021 internal code) and taxol lookup (PubChem CID 36314) was not informative for Eg5; the Eg5 literature searches were run after submit_conclusion so did not inform the call.

Lesson: with antimitotic candidates and atlas split 6/4, tub_mean/std/contrast magnitude alone cannot separate stabilizer vs Eg5 in this assay. The combination of already maximal nuc_solidity drop and nuc_dna elevation at 0.001 µM, plus flat DNA dose-response, plus close atlas tie should have kept Eg5 at ~0.4-0.5 and triggered spindle-polarity imaging before concluding.
what_was_right: Identified antimitotic arrest (no cell loss, density similar, low nuc_solidity/form_factor, high DNA content) and correctly excluded destabilizers, DNA damage, actin etc.
Microscopist candidates and atlas both flagged both stabilizers and Eg5 - the true ambiguity was captured
what_was_wrong: Treated tub_mean +28.5, tub_std +19.4, tub_glcm_contrast +40.2 and rho=+1.00 as stabilizer-selective; Eg5 monopolar asters produce same focal tubulin increase - no evidence in run supported selectivity, and literature comparison search had 0 hits

Discounted 4/10 Eg5 neighbors and e4 Eg5 candidacy; listed strong tub metrics as contradicting Eg5 when they do not - Eg5 inhibitors cause monopolar spindle arrest PMID 10542155 PMID 10973989 PMID 12323373
Ignored contradicting flat dose responses: nuc_dna_integrated rho 0.00 and frac_large_nucleus rho -0.40 argue against stabilizer graded polyploidy model
Based dose-dependency on n=4 with p=0, acquired only 4 of 8 doses, no replicates and no spindle-polarity imaging to distinguish bundles vs monopolar

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

APPROVED: The evidence supports the top MoA over the runner-up hypotheses. The tubulin signature is large, selective, and monotonically dose-dependent across four wells, including low doses, which favors a stabilizer over Eg5 or Aurora inhibition. The atlas shows a stabilizer majority, although the Eg5 similarity is close enough that the stated probability of 0.62 is reasonably calibrated rather than overconfident.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ-C** (no PubChem record shown)

Identity check: BBBC021 gives no structure for this compound (an internal code); name matches in PubChem would be unrelated compounds, so none is shown

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Eg5 inhibitors**.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth = Eg5 inhibitors. Submitted conclusion = Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62. Incorrect.

What the evidence got right:
- Correctly identified an antimitotic mitotic-arrest phenotype, not DNA damage, actin, protein synthesis/degradation, etc. This was supported by: density similar vs DMSO by microscopist, no cell loss - High dose w_246fbe6008 (1 µM) 295 cells, mid dose w_2eeef82f69 295 cells, low dose w_6d52bef633 416 cells - consistent with arrest not acute cytotoxicity; strongly decreased nuc_solidity z=-28.3 at 1 µM, -19.1 at 0.03 µM, -15.2 even at 0.001 µM and -15.6 at 0.3 µM plus decreased form_factor, and elevated nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.8 at 0.03 µM and +14.3 at 0.001 µM.
- describe_phenotype correctly kept both Microtubule stabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors (and Aurora) as candidates on 4 fields. compare_to_reference_atlas was also correctly equivocal: 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers, 4/10 Eg5 inhibitors. That near-tie should have been the central uncertainty.
- Correctly downweighted Microtubule destabilizers, Actin disruptors, DNA damage/replication based on increased not decreased tubulin metrics.

What misled and why:
- Over-interpretation of tubulin intensity/texture as stabilizer-specific. w_246fbe6008 tub_mean z=+28.5, tub_std z=+19.4 at 0.03 µM, tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2 at 1 µM, and dose_response rho=+1.00 p=0 for both tub_mean (e8) and tub_glcm_contrast (e11) over 4 wells/4 doses were taken as selective polymerization/bundling signature. In this image-based assay Eg5 inhibition producing monopolar asters with dense focal tubulin also drives very high tub_mean, tub_std and contrast. There was no direct literature in this run comparing the two phenotypes - PubMed search 'microtubule stabilizer vs Eg5 inhibitor phenotype' returned 0 hits - so the claim that this magnitude is discriminating was unsupported. I anchored on the extreme z=+40.2 and monotonic rho without considering the overlap.
- Under-weighting of Eg5 support. e4 included Eg5 inhibitors among microscopist candidates and e5 gave 4/10 Eg5 nearest references. In update_hypotheses I listed e2 and e11 as "contradicting" Eg5, but extreme tub contrast does not contradict Eg5; monastrol, the prototype small-molecule inhibitor of spindle bipolarity, produces monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest PMID 10542155, PMID 10973989, and is an allosteric inhibitor of Eg5 PMID 12323373, PMID 15665380, PMID 12525161. Image-based profiling alone is known to conflate these mitotic MoAs without spindle-pole resolution PMID 24997502.
- Ignoring flat/inconsistent DNA/large-nucleus dose responses that argued against a classic stabilizer polyploidy progression. nuc_dna_integrated rho=0.00 p=1 (e9) over the same 4 wells was flat - high already at the lowest dose tested - and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (e10) was non-significant negative. That does not support a graded stabilizer-induced G2/M->polyploidy increase and was not incorporated as contradicting evidence for stabilizers.
- Acquisition choices: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.0003-1 µM available but I only acquired 4 wells (0.001, 0.03, 0.3, 1 µM) with n=1 per dose. Dose_response with n=4 and reported p=0 is over-confident and cannot be interpreted as strong monotonic proof. No high-resolution confocal tubulin/DNA spindle imaging or phospho-histone H3 assay was acquired to distinguish stabilizer bundles/multipolar spindles from Eg5 monopolar spindles, which was explicitly noted in the "next_experiment_if_this_were_a_real_lab" but should have been done before submitting. Protocol lookup after unblinding confirmed AZ-C has no PubChem/ChemBL structure curated (BBBC021 internal code) and taxol lookup (PubChem CID 36314) was not informative for Eg5; the Eg5 literature searches were run after submit_conclusion so did not inform the call.

Lesson: with antimitotic candidates and atlas split 6/4, tub_mean/std/contrast magnitude alone cannot separate stabilizer vs Eg5 in this assay. The combination of already maximal nuc_solidity drop and nuc_dna elevation at 0.001 µM, plus flat DNA dose-response, plus close atlas tie should have kept Eg5 at ~0.4-0.5 and triggered spindle-polarity imaging before concluding.

What was right:
- Identified antimitotic arrest (no cell loss, density similar, low nuc_solidity/form_factor, high DNA content) and correctly excluded destabilizers, DNA damage, actin etc.
- Microscopist candidates and atlas both flagged both stabilizers and Eg5 - the true ambiguity was captured

What was wrong or missed:
- Treated tub_mean +28.5, tub_std +19.4, tub_glcm_contrast +40.2 and rho=+1.00 as stabilizer-selective; Eg5 monopolar asters produce same focal tubulin increase - no evidence in run supported selectivity, and literature comparison search had 0 hits
- Discounted 4/10 Eg5 neighbors and e4 Eg5 candidacy; listed strong tub metrics as contradicting Eg5 when they do not - Eg5 inhibitors cause monopolar spindle arrest PMID 10542155 PMID 10973989 PMID 12323373
- Ignored contradicting flat dose responses: nuc_dna_integrated rho 0.00 and frac_large_nucleus rho -0.40 argue against stabilizer graded polyploidy model
- Based dose-dependency on n=4 with p=0, acquired only 4 of 8 doses, no replicates and no spindle-polarity imaging to distinguish bundles vs monopolar

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution confocal tubulin/DNA co-stain with pericentrin/gamma-tubulin to count spindle poles (monopolar vs bipolar/multipolar bundles) plus phospho-H3 mitotic index across 8-point dose range; cell-free tubulin polymerization assay to test direct stabilizer activity vs negative in Eg5 inhibition.
